name: mlx5e_xsk_skb_from_cqe_mpwrq_linear
prose: Builds (or consumes) the packet for one received multi-packet WQE entry on an XSK (AF_XDP zero-copy) RQ in linear mode (xsk/rx.c:249-304; the packet name mlx5e_xsk_skb_from_cqe_mpwrq is not the real name and the slice cut the head). If cqe_bcnt is larger than rq->hw_mtu it increments the oversize_pkts_sw_drop counter and returns NULL. A non-zero head_offset only triggers WARN_ON_ONCE and is otherwise ignored. It stores the CQE in the XSK buffer's mlx5e_xdp_buff, sets the buffer size to cqe_bcnt, syncs the DMA buffer for the CPU and prefetches the data. If an XDP program is attached (rcu_dereference(rq->xdp_prog)) and mlx5e_xdp_handle returns true (the packet was consumed by XDP), it marks the page in wi->skip_release_bitmap when the RQ's XDP_XMIT flag was set (clearing the flag) and returns NULL. Otherwise (no program, or XDP_PASS) it returns mlx5e_xsk_construct_skb(rq, &mxbuf->xdp), which copies the data into a new skb and returns NULL if that allocation fails.
note: Packet name wrong; real function mlx5e_xsk_skb_from_cqe_mpwrq_linear (xsk/rx.c:249-304). The prior prose took mxbuf as a parameter; it is derived from wi->alloc_units.xsk_buffs[page_idx]. Old reviewers mechanical only (right).

name: mlx5e_accel_tx_begin
prose: Runs the transmit-side offload preprocessing for an skb on an mlx5e queue (en_accel.h:129-169; static inline; slice cut the head). Each of the steps below exists only if the corresponding kernel config option is enabled. If the skb is GSO with SKB_GSO_UDP_L4 it first calls mlx5e_udp_gso_handle_tx_skb, which modifies the skb's UDP header. Then, in order: if the skb is TLS-offloaded it calls mlx5e_ktls_handle_tx_skb(dev, sq, skb, &state->tls) (which may post WQEs on sq) and returns false if that returns false; if PSP offload applies it calls mlx5e_psp_handle_tx_skb(dev, skb, &state->psp_st) and returns false on failure; if the SQ has the IPsec state bit and the skb has xfrm offload it calls mlx5e_ipsec_handle_tx_skb(dev, skb, &state->ipsec) and returns false on failure; if the skb is MACsec-offloaded it calls mlx5e_macsec_handle_tx_skb(priv->macsec, skb) (which takes no accel state pointer) and returns false on failure. It returns true when no handler failed. Only the TLS path takes sq as an argument.
note: Reviewers: original (omits UDP GSO header update and possible WQEs on success) right: 134-135, 138-142; round-2 (prose says every offload may emit WQEs to sq; only TLS takes sq) right: 140, 147, 154, 163; round-15 (MACsec handler receives no state pointer, so it cannot fill state) right: 163. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head.

name: mlx5e_ktls_rx_handle_resync_list
prose: Posts pending kTLS RX resync static-params WQEs to the async ICOSQ (ktls_rx.c:747-811; the packet item is only the tail of this function and its name was elided). It returns false at once if the async ICOSQ is not enabled. Otherwise, under the resync list lock it moves up to 'budget' entries from ktls_resync->list to a local list (i counts the entries moved) and clears MLX5E_SQ_STATE_PENDING_TLS_RX_RESYNC if the shared list is then empty. Under the ICOSQ lock it then, for each moved entry in turn, takes that entry's lock and calls post_static_params; if that returns an error (the queue is full) it stops, otherwise it removes the entry from the local list and remembers its control segment. If any WQE was posted it rings the doorbell once for the last one. It adds the number posted (j) to the tls_resync_res_ok statistic (through the cursor priv_rx, which is also used when no entry was moved). If entries remain on the local list it puts them back at the front of the shared list, sets the pending bit again and counts tls_resync_res_retry. It returns whether i == budget, i.e. whether the number of entries taken from the shared list equals the budget; this is not the same as the number actually posted.
note: Item was the tail of mlx5e_ktls_rx_handle_resync_list; fixed under the real name per rule 6. The old prose said true means every WQE was posted; the return is i == budget where i counts entries moved to the local list, regardless of posting success.

name: MLX5E_DECLARE_STATS_GRP_OP_NUM_STATS(macsec_hw)
prose: Generated function mlx5e_stats_grp_macsec_hw_num_stats(struct mlx5e_priv *priv) (macsec_stats.c, declared with MLX5E_DECLARE_STATS_GRP_OP_NUM_STATS(macsec_hw), which expands to 'int mlx5e_stats_grp_macsec_hw_num_stats(struct mlx5e_priv *priv)'). It returns 0 if priv->macsec is NULL, and 0 if mlx5e_is_macsec_device(priv->mdev) is false; otherwise it returns NUM_MACSEC_HW_COUNTERS, the number of entries of mlx5e_macsec_hw_stats_desc (8 entries: rx/tx packets, bytes, dropped packets and dropped bytes). It has no side effects.
note: Name written as the macro invocation per rule 5; the real generated name comes from MLX5E_STATS_GRP_OP(grp, name) = mlx5e_stats_grp_<grp>_<name> (en_stats.h:83-86). Old prose unreviewed; checked against macsec_stats.c:12-30.

name: mlx5e_fs_vlan_rx_kill_vid
prose: Removes a VLAN id from the mlx5e flow-steering state (en_fs.c:511-532; slice cut the head). If fs->vlan is NULL it logs 'Vlan doesn't exist' and returns -EINVAL without changing anything. For proto ETH_P_8021Q it clears the vid bit in fs->vlan->active_cvlans and deletes the matching C-tag VLAN rule with mlx5e_fs_del_vlan_rule. For ETH_P_8021AD it clears the bit in active_svlans, deletes the S-tag rule, and calls netdev_update_features(netdev) under netdev_lock/netdev_unlock. For any other proto it changes nothing. In every case other than the NULL-vlan one it reaches the final 'return 0'. This function does not itself call mlx5e_vport_context_update_vlans.
note: Reviewers: original (no return 0 or -EOPNOTSUPP; falls off the end for known/unknown proto) WRONG: 531 returns 0 after the if/else-if chain; round-15 (omits mlx5e_vport_context_update_vlans side effect for 8021Q deletion) WRONG for this function: no such call at 511-532 (any such effect would be inside mlx5e_fs_del_vlan_rule, which I did not read). 0 right, 2 wrong. Slice cut the head.

name: MLX5E_DECLARE_STATS_GRP_OP_FILL_STATS(ptp)
prose: Generated function mlx5e_stats_grp_ptp_fill_stats(struct mlx5e_priv *priv, u64 **data) (en_stats.c; declared with MLX5E_DECLARE_STATS_GRP_OP_FILL_STATS(ptp)). If neither priv->tx_ptp_opened nor priv->rx_ptp_opened is set it writes nothing. Otherwise it appends the NUM_PTP_CH_STATS channel counters from priv->ptp_stats.ch; if tx_ptp_opened it then appends, for each tc below priv->max_opened_tc, the NUM_PTP_SQ_STATS counters of ptp_stats.sq[tc] and afterwards, again for each tc, the NUM_PTP_CQ_STATS counters of ptp_stats.cq[tc]; if rx_ptp_opened it appends the NUM_PTP_RQ_STATS counters of ptp_stats.rq. Each counter is written through mlx5e_ethtool_put_stat, advancing *data. data must have room for all of them. It returns nothing.
note: Name written as the macro invocation per rule 5. Rechecked against the body printed from en_stats.c (the function immediately follows its declaration macro).

name: MLX5E_DECLARE_STATS_GRP_OP_NUM_STATS(vport)
prose: Generated function mlx5e_stats_grp_vport_num_stats(struct mlx5e_priv *priv) (en_stats.c:786-790). It returns NUM_VPORT_COUNTERS (the number of entries of vport_stats_desc, which is 20: 12 Ethernet and 8 RDMA unicast/multicast counters) plus NUM_VPORT_LOOPBACK_COUNTERS(priv->mdev), which is 2 (entries of vport_loopback_stats_desc) when the device has the vport_counter_local_loopback capability and 0 otherwise. So it returns 20 or 22. It has no side effects.
note: Round-15 reviewer (prose wrongly says NUM_VPORT_COUNTERS is 2; vport_stats_desc has 16 entries, so 16 or 18) is right that 2 is wrong but its own number is also wrong: counting en_stats.c:731-772 gives 20 entries, so 20 or 22. Rated mixed.

name: MLX5E_DECLARE_STATS_GRP_OP_FILL_STRS(vport)
prose: Generated function mlx5e_stats_grp_vport_fill_strings(struct mlx5e_priv *priv, u8 **data) (en_stats.c:792-801). It appends, with ethtool_puts, the format string of each of the 20 vport_stats_desc entries and then, when the device has the vport_counter_local_loopback capability, the 2 vport_loopback_stats_desc strings, advancing *data. data must have room for 20 or 22 strings, matching the num_stats function. It returns nothing.
note: Round-15 reviewer (claims 2 vport strings; actual NUM_VPORT_COUNTERS is 16, so 16 or 18) is mixed: the count of 2 in the old prose was wrong, but the actual array has 20 entries, not 16 (en_stats.c:731-772).

name: MLX5E_DECLARE_STATS_GRP_OP_FILL_STATS(vport)
prose: Generated function mlx5e_stats_grp_vport_fill_stats(struct mlx5e_priv *priv, u64 **data) (en_stats.c:803-818). It appends, with mlx5e_ethtool_put_stat, the 64-bit big-endian counter for each of the 20 vport_stats_desc entries read from priv->stats.vport.query_vport_out, then the 2 loopback counters when the vport_counter_local_loopback capability is present, advancing *data. data must have room for 20 or 22 values. It reads the last query result and does not issue a new query (that is done by the separate update_stats op). It returns nothing.
note: Round-15 reviewer (precondition says room for 2/4 stats; actual count is 16/18) is mixed: old count wrong, but actual is 20/22 (20 entries in vport_stats_desc, en_stats.c:731-772).

name: parse_cls_flower
prose: Parses a TC flower classifier into an mlx5 flow spec and applies the eswitch minimum-inline check (en_tc.c:3155-3198; slice cut the head). It sets local inner and outer match levels to MLX5_MATCH_NONE and calls __parse_cls_flower(priv, flow, spec, f, filter_dev, &inner_level, &outer_level), keeping its return value in err. The non-tunnel match level is the inner level if it is not NONE, else the outer level. For an eswitch flow, when err is 0, the representor's vport is not the uplink and the eswitch inline mode is set and lower than the non-tunnel match level, it sets an extack message, warns and returns -EOPNOTSUPP; that is the only early return. In every other case, including when __parse_cls_flower failed, it stores the inner and outer match levels in flow->attr and returns err (0 on success, or the error of __parse_cls_flower).
note: Round-15 reviewer (on __parse_cls_flower failure the error is returned without storing match levels) is WRONG: 3193-3194 store the match levels before 'return err' for every path except the -EOPNOTSUPP one. Slice cut the head; real function 3155-3198.

name: parse_branch_ctrl
prose: Sets up the true/false branch attributes for a TC action that supports branching (en_tc.c:3976-4018; slice cut the head). If tc_act->get_branch_ctrl is NULL it returns 0 immediately without reading or changing attr or jump_state. Otherwise it gets the true and false branch controls from the action and allocates the true-branch attribute with alloc_branch_attr (an error is returned as is); if that left a non-zero jump count it sets jump_state->jumping_attr to the true branch (so jump_state may already be modified before a later failure). It then allocates the false-branch attribute; if that fails it frees attr->branch_true (without resetting the pointer to NULL) and returns the error, leaving jump_state->jumping_attr possibly already set. On success it sets jumping_attr to the false branch if it is not set yet and the count is non-zero, stores the new jump count in jump_state, adds the COUNT action bit to attr->action, sets USE_ACT_STATS on the flow and returns 0.
note: Reviewers: original (on failure only branch_true is freed; branch_false is not allocated) right: 4014-4015; round-2 (returns 0 when get_branch_ctrl is NULL; branch_true not NULL-ed after free) right: 3985-3986, 4015; round-15 (on false-branch failure jumping_attr may already be set, contradicting 'jump_state unchanged') right: 3995-3996. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head.

name: mlx5_eswitch_add_termtbl_rule
prose: Adds an FDB flow rule whose vport destinations go through termination tables, falling back to the plain rule on failure (eswitch_offloads_termtbl.c:245-338; the packet name mlx5_eswitch_termtbl_process_dest is not the real name and the slice cut the head). It moves the VLAN-push actions from *flow_act into a local term_tbl_act (mlx5_eswitch_termtbl_actions_move) and adds FWD_DEST. For each destination of type VPORT (other types are skipped) it sets or clears the packet-reformat action according to the matching attr->dests[] entry's ENCAP flag, gets or creates a termination table for it (mlx5_eswitch_termtbl_get_create; an error is warned and goes to revert_changes), records the table in attr->dests[n].termtbl and rewrites that destination into a flow-table destination pointing at the termination table. If no destination was converted it goes to revert_changes. Otherwise it clears the packet-reformat from flow_act, sets FLOW_ACT_IGNORE_FLOW_LEVEL and calls mlx5_add_flow_rules(fdb, spec, flow_act, dest, num_dest); if that returns an error it goes to revert_changes, else it returns the rule. revert_changes moves the VLAN-push actions back into *flow_act, clears each attr->dests[].termtbl, restores the corresponding dest[] entries to vport destinations and releases the termination tables (mlx5_eswitch_termtbl_put), then calls mlx5_add_flow_rules again with the original actions and returns that result (a valid handle or an ERR_PTR). Note dest[] and *flow_act are modified in place.
note: Packet name wrong and slice cut the head; real function mlx5_eswitch_add_termtbl_rule (eswitch_offloads_termtbl.c:245-338), read in full. Old reviewers mechanical only (right).

name: mlx5_do_bond
prose: Re-evaluates and applies the LAG (bonding) state of an mlx5 device (lag/lag.c:1152-1247; slice cut the head; returns nothing). It returns without any LAG change if the P1 device index is negative, or if LAG is ready and the P1 device is in multipath mode. do_bond is false when LAG is not ready, else it is the tracker's is_bonded and the prerequisite check. If do_bond is true and LAG is not active it removes the devices (for shared FDB or RoCE LAG), activates LAG in RoCE or SR-IOV mode, and on an activation failure re-adds the devices (and, for shared FDB, reloads the IB reps) and returns without the notifier call or the vport speed update. When activation succeeded: in the RoCE-LAG case it clears the IB-adev disable flag, rescans the drivers and enables RoCE on the other functions; in the shared-FDB case it clears the flag, rescans and reloads IB reps on each device, and if any reload fails it sets the flag again, rescans, deactivates LAG, re-adds the devices, reloads the reps, logs 'Failed to enable lag' and returns early. The driver rescan and RoCE steps therefore happen only in those two branches, not for every successful activation. For active-backup it then notifies the lag notifier chain with the active netdev (and dev_put's it) and finally updates the vport aggregate speed. If LAG is not being newly activated it modifies LAG and updates the speed when mlx5_lag_should_modify_lag, or resets the speed and disables LAG when mlx5_lag_should_disable_lag.
note: Reviewers: original (omits early returns for invalid index and multipath mode) right: 1162-1171; round-2 (omits shared_fdb IB-rep reload failure rollback returning without notifier or speed update) right: 1218-1227; round-15 (rescan/clear only in roce_lag/shared_fdb branches, not all activation successes) right: 1199-1228. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head.

name: mlx5_lag_fib_route_event
prose: Handles a FIB route add/replace/delete event for mlx5 multipath LAG (lag/mp.c:155-226; slice cut the head; returns nothing). It returns without effect if the P1 device index is negative. For FIB_EVENT_ENTRY_DEL it clears mp->fib.mfi if that is the deleted fib_info and returns. Otherwise it rejects (debug message, return) an entry for a different prefix when a tracked multipath entry exists with a shorter-or-equal prefix length and is not of lower priority value. It finds the first two nexthop netdevs that belong to this LAG (mlx5_lag_get_next_fib_dev). With no such nexthop it clears mp->fib.mfi if the tracked destination equals this entry's destination and length (no-nexthop clearing) and returns. If both nexthops are the same device it warns that multipath offload does not support it and returns. With exactly one nexthop it acts only if LAG is active: it computes the device index of that nexthop, calls mlx5_lag_set_port_affinity (which itself does nothing unless the LAG is in multipath mode) and records the route with mlx5_lag_fib_set; if LAG is not active it does nothing. With two distinct nexthops, if no route is tracked yet and LAG is not active it activates LAG in multipath mode (the result is ignored); then it sets normal affinity (again a no-op unless multipath) and records the route with mlx5_lag_fib_set.
note: Reviewers: original (omits no-nexthop clearing and same-device warning; single-port affinity only when LAG active) right: 190-214; round-2 (in the single-nexthop case mlx5_lag_fib_set is called only when LAG is active) right: 202-213; round-15 (set_port_affinity no-ops unless LAG is multipath, not merely active) right: mp.c:60-61 checks __mlx5_lag_is_multipath. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head.

name: mlx5_ipsec_fs_roce_rx_create
prose: Creates the RoCE IPsec RX flow tables, groups and rules for one IP family (lib/ipsec_fs_roce.c, 'int mlx5_ipsec_fs_roce_rx_create(struct mlx5_core_dev *mdev, struct mlx5_ipsec_fs *ipsec_roce, struct mlx5_flow_namespace *ns, struct mlx5_flow_destination *default_dst, u32 family, u32 level, u32 prio)' at about lines 706-815; the packet item had a truncated name and the slice shows only the later part). It returns 0 without doing anything if ipsec_roce is NULL. It picks the IPv4 or IPv6 RX state by family, creates a 2-entry flow table in ns (an error is returned directly), allocates a flow-group input buffer (-ENOMEM), creates the RoCE flow group matching ip_protocol and udp_dport and a second group for the miss rule (each failure logs and unwinds), then for an MPV slave creates the MPV alias tables (ipsec_fs_roce_rx_mpv_create) or otherwise a 1-entry RDMA flow table in roce->ns_rdma (level 1 for AF_INET), and finally sets up the rules (ipsec_fs_roce_rx_rule_setup). On success it frees the buffer and returns 0. Failures unwind in reverse order through the labels (rules setup failure destroys the MPV tables for an MPV slave and the RDMA table, then the miss group, the RoCE group, the buffer and the first table), and return the error. Note that on the rule-setup failure path mlx5_destroy_flow_table(roce->ft_rdma) is called after the MPV tables were destroyed, also for an MPV slave.
note: Packet name truncated; slice starts inside the function. Real function mlx5_ipsec_fs_roce_rx_create. I read the head (706-742) and everything from 742 to the end of the function. Old reviewers mechanical only (right).

name: mlx5_vxlan_reset_to_default
prose: Header-only stub (lib/vxlan.h:60): when CONFIG_VXLAN is not enabled, 'static inline void mlx5_vxlan_reset_to_default(struct mlx5_vxlan *vxlan) { return; }' does nothing. When CONFIG_VXLAN is enabled this header contains only the declaration 'void mlx5_vxlan_reset_to_default(struct mlx5_vxlan *vxlan);' (line 55); the implementation is not in this file, so this slice cannot describe what it does in that configuration.
note: Reviewer note (only the CONFIG_VXLAN-disabled stub is a no-op; the enabled implementation is just declared) is right and is reflected here. The previous action was 'dropped'; a real (trivial) function body exists in the header, so it is kept as a fix limited to the stub.

name: mlx5_fs_fte_get_hws_actions
prose: Builds the HW-steering rule action list for a flow table entry (fs_hws.c:739-1069; the packet name mlx5_fs_hws_create_action is not the real name and the slice shows only the middle and tail). It allocates *ractions (MLX5_FLOW_CONTEXT_ACTION_MAX rule actions), a temporary fs_actions array and a destination-action array with kcalloc (-ENOMEM on failure, undoing the earlier allocations). It then appends actions in the fixed order the comment lists (decap, remove header, pop VLAN, modify header, push VLAN, reformat, counter, tag, ASO meter, drop, forward destinations, destination array, last), taking each from the cached per-namespace actions or creating a new one; the actions created specifically for this rule are tracked in fs_actions. Any failure (missing resource, unsupported combination, -EOPNOTSUPP when the action arrays are full or a destination array cannot be built, -ENOMEM) goes to free_actions, which destroys the actions created so far and frees all temporary arrays and *ractions (set to NULL) and returns the error. On success it frees the destination array, stores num_fs_actions and the fs_actions array in fte->fs_hws_rule (so they live until the rule is deleted) and returns 0.
note: Packet name wrong; real function mlx5_fs_fte_get_hws_actions (fs_hws.c:739-1069). I read only its head (739-800) and tail (1010-1069) and the label structure; I did not read the middle (about 800-1010) that builds each individual action, so the per-action behaviour is summarised from the comment and goto structure only.

name: mlx5hws_matcher_resize_rule_move
prose: Moves one rule from a matcher being resized to its destination matcher (steering/hws/matcher.c, 'int mlx5hws_matcher_resize_rule_move(struct mlx5hws_matcher *src_matcher, struct mlx5hws_rule *rule, struct mlx5hws_rule_attr *attr)' at about lines 1272-1293; the slice shows only its body). It returns -EINVAL, after an error log, if the source matcher is not in resize (mlx5hws_matcher_is_in_resize false) and -EINVAL, after a log, if rule->matcher is not src_matcher. Otherwise it returns the value of mlx5hws_rule_move_hws_add(rule, attr), so it does not return 0 itself on success; the result is whatever that call returns.
note: Slice began inside the function; fixed under the real name per rule 6 (read the whole function). Old prose said it returns 0 after moving, but the success value is that of mlx5hws_rule_move_hws_add.

name: dr_dump_rule_action_mem
prose: Writes one debug-dump record for a rule action to a seq_file (steering/sws/dr_dbg.c:208-487; the packet name dr_dump_rule_action is not the real name and the slice cut the head). buff must be a buffer of MLX5DR_DEBUG_DUMP_BUFF_LENGTH bytes and action_mem->action a valid action. It switches on action->action_type; for each handled type (drop, flow table, counter, and the other action kinds in the switch: the table I read first-hand covers DROP, FT, CTR and MATCH_RANGE, the other cases follow the same pattern) it formats a comma-separated record (record type, the action id, the rule id and type-specific ids) into buff with snprintf and prints it with mlx5dr_dbg_dump_data_print. If snprintf returns a negative value it returns that value, and if the print call returns non-zero it returns that status; otherwise it breaks out. An action type not listed in the switch (default) returns 0 and writes nothing. After a successful case it returns 0.
note: Packet name wrong; slice cut the head. Real function dr_dump_rule_action_mem (208-487, 280 lines). I read the head (208-262) and the tail (455-487) plus the list of return statements; I did NOT read the middle cases (about 262-455) individually.

name: mlx5_cmd_dr_create_fte
prose: Creates a software-steering (DR) rule for a flow table entry (steering/sws/fs_dr.c:252-632; the packet name mlx5_fs_dr_create_fte is not the real name, and it returns int, not a pointer). If the flow table is a firmware termination table it delegates to the firmware create_fte handler and returns its result unchanged. Otherwise it allocates arrays for rule actions, rule-owned DR actions and terminating actions with kcalloc (-ENOMEM, undoing earlier allocations), builds the DR action list from the entry's actions and destinations in a fixed order (several action kinds, including packet reformat/encap, modify header, VLAN, counters, destinations that may form a multi-destination action), and creates the rule with mlx5dr_rule_create on the group's matcher with the entry's match value. Any failure along the way (-ENOMEM, -EOPNOTSUPP or other error codes from action construction, or -EINVAL if mlx5dr_rule_create returns NULL) goes to free_actions, which destroys the DR actions created so far in reverse order, frees the temporary arrays, logs 'Failed to create dr rule err(%d)' and returns the error. On success it frees the temporary arrays, stores the rule, the count and the DR actions in fte->fs_dr_rule (the actions live until the rule is deleted) and returns 0.
note: Packet name wrong and the old prose said it returns a pointer; the function returns int (0 or negative error). Slice cut the head. I read the head (252-300) and tail (596-632) and the label structure; I did not read the middle (300-596) that builds each action.

name: mlxbf_gige_start_xmit
prose: ndo_start_xmit of the Mellanox BlueField GigE driver (mlxbf_gige_tx.c:191-284; the packet item was only the tail of this function and its name was elided). It always returns NETDEV_TX_OK. If skb->len exceeds MLXBF_GIGE_DEFAULT_BUF_SZ or skb_linearize fails it frees the skb, counts tx_dropped and returns. If the payload crosses a DMA page boundary it allocates a new aligned skb (mlxbf_gige_alloc_skb, which also returns the DMA address), copies the data and frees the original; an allocation failure frees the original, counts tx_dropped and returns. Otherwise it maps the original skb with dma_map_single (a mapping error frees the skb, counts tx_dropped and returns). It then takes the next TX WQE (mlxbf_gige_update_tx_wqe_next), writes the DMA address in word 0 and the packet length in word 1, stores the skb at tx_skb[tx_pi % tx_q_entries] and increments tx_pi under priv->lock (spin_lock_irqsave), writes the TX producer index register (after wmb) only when netdev_xmit_more() is false, and if no TX buffer is left available it stops the queue and schedules NAPI to process completions.
note: Item was a fragment of mlxbf_gige_start_xmit; fixed under the real name per rule 6. The old prose covered only the tail (no early drop paths).

name: MLXSW_ITEM8(_type, _cname, _iname, _offset, _shift, _sizebits)
prose: Macro (item.h:309-325) that defines, for each use, a static struct mlxsw_item and a getter/setter pair of static inline functions mlxsw_<type>_<cname>_<iname>_get(const char *buf) and mlxsw_<type>_<cname>_<iname>_set(char *buf, <u8|u16|u32|u64> val). MLXSW_ITEM16, MLXSW_ITEM32 and MLXSW_ITEM64 are the same with wider types. The getter reads the item through __mlxsw_item_getN with index 0: it reads the big-endian value at byte offset 'offset' (for the 8-bit variant a plain byte), shifts it right by 'shift', masks it to 'size.bits' bits, and (only if no_real_shift is set, which these non-indexed macros leave false) shifts it back. The setter shifts val left by 'shift', masks it to the field and replaces only that field of the stored value, leaving the other bits unchanged; bits of val beyond the field width are discarded. The offset must be a multiple of the access size, otherwise __mlxsw_item_offset prints an error and calls BUG(). buf must have the bytes at the item's offset available.
note: Macro-generated functions: name is the macro definition head per rule 5; the prose names the generated functions and the helpers in item.h:30-230 that I read. The old prose ('shifted right...') is consistent; the BUG on misaligned offsets was missing.

name: MLXSW_ITEM8_INDEXED(_type, _cname, _iname, _offset, _shift, _sizebits, _step, _instepoffset, _norealshift)
prose: Macro (item.h:327-352) defining an indexed item: a static struct mlxsw_item with step, in_step_offset and no_real_shift, plus mlxsw_<type>_<cname>_<iname>_get(const char *buf, unsigned short index) and _set(char *buf, unsigned short index, u8 val). MLXSW_ITEM16_INDEXED, MLXSW_ITEM32_INDEXED and MLXSW_ITEM64_INDEXED are the same for wider types. The accessors use byte offset 'offset + step * index + in_step_offset' (divided by the type size, which must divide offset, step and in_step_offset or __mlxsw_item_offset calls BUG(); a non-zero index with step 0 also calls BUG()). The getter reads the field, shifts and masks it to 'size.bits', and shifts it back left if no_real_shift is true; the setter shifts val left unless no_real_shift is true, masks it, and replaces only that field. The caller must provide a buffer containing the addressed bytes; there is no bounds check on index.
note: Macro-generated functions; name is the macro head per rule 5. Behaviour taken from __mlxsw_item_offset/get/set in item.h:30-230.

name: MLXSW_ITEM32_LP(_type, _cname, _offset1, _shift1, _offset2, _shift2)
prose: Macro (item.h:377-405) defining a local-port accessor pair built from two 32-bit items: 'local_port' (8 bits, LOCAL_PORT_LSB_SIZE, at _offset1/_shift1) and 'lp_msb' (2 bits, LOCAL_PORT_MSB_SIZE, at _offset2/_shift2). The generated mlxsw_<type>_<cname>_local_port_get(const char *buf) returns (lp_msb << 8) + local_port. The generated _local_port_set(char *buf, u32 val) writes the low 8 bits of val to the local_port item and val >> 8 to the lp_msb item (the setter for each item masks to its field width, so bits of val above bit 9 are dropped); other bits of the containers are preserved. The same alignment BUG() conditions as the other items apply.
note: Macro-generated functions; name is the macro head per rule 5.

name: MLXSW_ITEM_BUF(_type, _cname, _iname, _offset, _sizebytes)
prose: Macro (item.h:429-452) defining three accessors for a fixed-size byte buffer inside a container: mlxsw_<type>_<cname>_<iname>_memcpy_from(const char *buf, char *dst) copies exactly size.bytes bytes from buf + offset into dst; _memcpy_to(char *buf, const char *src) copies exactly size.bytes from src into buf + offset; and _data(char *buf) returns a pointer to buf + offset (no copy). MLXSW_ITEM_BUF_INDEXED adds an index argument and uses offset + step*index + in_step_offset. There is no bounds checking: buf must hold at least offset + size.bytes bytes, and dst/src must be at least size.bytes long; a non-zero index with step 0 calls BUG().
note: Macro-generated functions; name is the macro head per rule 5.

name: MLXSW_ITEM_BIT_ARRAY(_type, _cname, _iname, _offset, _sizebytes, _element_size) -- getter
prose: Generated getter mlxsw_<type>_<cname>_<iname>_get(const char *buf, u16 index) of MLXSW_ITEM_BIT_ARRAY (item.h:534-557, helper __mlxsw_item_bit_array_get): it returns the element_size-bit element number 'index' of a byte array of size.bytes bytes at 'offset', counting elements from the end of the array (element 0 is in the last byte, i.e. big-endian element order). If index is above the maximum ((size.bytes*8)/element_size - 1) it warns once and uses index 0. The byte is shifted right by the element's position in its byte and masked to element_size bits, and returned as u8. It BUG()s if offset is not a multiple of 4 or 8 is not a multiple of element_size.
note: Macro-generated function; name is the macro head per rule 5, suffix indicates the getter. Behaviour from item.h:211-247. Old reviewers mechanical only.

name: MLXSW_ITEM_BIT_ARRAY(_type, _cname, _iname, _offset, _sizebytes, _element_size) -- setter
prose: Generated setter mlxsw_<type>_<cname>_<iname>_set(char *buf, u16 index, u8 val) of MLXSW_ITEM_BIT_ARRAY (helper __mlxsw_item_bit_array_set, item.h:249-262): it stores val into the element_size-bit element number 'index' (same end-relative element numbering and same index clamp to 0 with a one-time warning as the getter) by shifting val to the element's position in its byte, masking it, and replacing only that element's bits in the byte, leaving the rest of the byte unchanged. Bits of val above element_size are discarded. It BUG()s on a misaligned offset or an element_size that does not divide 8. It returns nothing (the macro's 'return' of a void call).
note: Macro-generated function; name is the macro head per rule 5, suffix indicates the setter.

name: mlxsw_pci_cqe_item_helpers(name, v0, v1, v2)
prose: Macro (pci_hw.h:114-139) that defines, for each use, two static inline functions: mlxsw_pci_cqe_<name>_get(enum mlxsw_pci_cqe_v v, char *cqe) returning u32, and mlxsw_pci_cqe_<name>_set(enum mlxsw_pci_cqe_v v, char *cqe, u32 val). The getter dispatches on the CQE version v: MLXSW_PCI_CQE_V1 calls mlxsw_pci_cqe<v1>_<name>_get(cqe), MLXSW_PCI_CQE_V2 calls the v2 variant, and every other value (V0 and any out-of-range value, through the shared default label) calls the v0 variant. The setter does the same dispatch to the matching _set(cqe, val). The v0/v1/v2 macro arguments are the suffixes that name the per-version item accessors (for example 0, 12 or 2 for cqe0, cqe12, cqe2). cqe must point to a CQE buffer large enough for the selected item; the called item setters preserve the other bits of the container.
note: Macro-generated functions; name is the macro head per rule 5. Old prose consistent with the macro; I checked the dispatch and default-label behaviour at pci_hw.h:116-139.

name: mlxsw_sp_port_create
prose: Creates and registers the net_device and software state of one Spectrum port (spectrum.c:1457-1744; slice cut the head). It first maps the port to its module (mlxsw_sp_port_module_map; failure returns the error directly), then performs, in order, SWID assignment, port-label lookup, core port init, netdev and per-CPU stats allocation, MAC address setup, system-port mapping, speed-by-width and max-speed queries, MTU, admin status, buffers, ETS, TC multicast mode, DCB, FIDs, qdiscs, VLAN clear, NVE, PVID, default VLAN creation and VLAN classification, stores the port in mlxsw_sp->ports[local_port], sets the overheat initial value and calls register_netdev. Each failure logs and jumps to a label that undoes only the steps that have their own teardown, in reverse: VLAN classification, port VLAN destroy, NVE, qdisc, FIDs, DCB, TC multicast mode, buffers, per-CPU stats, free_netdev, core port fini, SWID reset to the disabled value and module unmap. The configuration-only steps for admin status, MTU, max speed, speed-by-width, system-port mapping, ETS and the overheat initial value have no undo action on the error path. On success it schedules the periodic hardware-stats work and returns 0; on failure it returns the failing step's error.
note: Round-15 reviewer (cleanup of admin status, MTU, max speed, speed-by-width, system-port mapping, ETS and overheat init value is not done) is right: those labels (1703-1729) fall through without any teardown call. Slice cut the head; real function 1457-1744. I read the head and the whole error/label block, and relied on the goto list for the middle steps.

name: mlxsw_sp_netdevice_port_upper_event
prose: Handles upper-device change notifications for a Spectrum port (spectrum.c:4713-4867; slice cut the head; returns an int error). For NETDEV_PRECHANGEUPPER it returns -EINVAL for an upper that is not VLAN, LAG, bridge, OVS, macvlan or L3 master, then, when linking, runs a series of checks, returning -EOPNOTSUPP or -EINVAL with an extack message for unsupported combinations (a bridge with an unoffloaded VXLAN, VLAN on LAG or OVS ports, unknown or 802.1ad bridge VLAN protocols, non-802.1q VLAN uppers, VLAN uppers on a locked port), and returning whatever error mlxsw_sp_netdevice_validate_uppers returns when the upper already has uppers (an arbitrary errno, not only -EINVAL/-EOPNOTSUPP); unlinking passes. For NETDEV_CHANGEUPPER it joins or leaves a bridge (join error returned; leave optionally replays deslavement), joins or leaves a LAG (join error returned), joins or leaves OVS (join error returned), deletes the macvlan RIF when a macvlan is removed, and for a VLAN upper that is a bridge port and is being unlinked removes the port from that bridge. Join failures can return an error without setting an extack message. There is no VLAN-join call in this function. Other events do nothing and it returns 0.
note: Reviewers: original (CHANGEUPPER join failures may return errno without extack) right: 4820-4836, 4846; round-2 (PRECHANGEUPPER can propagate arbitrary errno from validate_uppers) right: 4754-4758; round-15 (omits mlxsw_sp_port_vlan_join failure return on CHANGEUPPER for a VLAN upper) WRONG for this code: the VLAN upper branch (4852-4862) only handles the leave case and has no join call. 2 right, 1 wrong. Slice cut the head; real function 4713-4867.

name: mlxsw_sp_counter_resources_register
prose: Registers the flow-counter devlink resources of a Spectrum device (spectrum_cnt.c:241-304; the packet name counter_pool_resources_register is not the real name and the slice cut the head). The caller holds the devlink instance lock (devl_resource_register is used). It returns -EIO if the COUNTER_POOL_SIZE or COUNTER_BANK_SIZE core resource is not valid. It registers the top-level counters resource with the pool size, then registers one sub-resource per entry of mlxsw_sp_counter_sub_pools sized at its bank_count * bank_size, truncated so that the cumulative size does not exceed the pool size; any devl_resource_register failure returns its error immediately (earlier resources stay registered). Finally it returns -EINVAL (with a WARN_ON) if the total configured bank count exceeds pool_size / bank_size + 1, else 0.
note: Packet name wrong and slice cut the head; real function mlxsw_sp_counter_resources_register (spectrum_cnt.c:241). Old reviewers mechanical only (right).

name: mlxsw_sp_fid_rfid_port_vid_map
prose: Maps a {port, VID} pair to an rFID (router FID) (spectrum_fid.c:1415-1463; slice cut the head). It adds {local_port, vid} to the FID's port-VID list (a failure is returned as is). It then calls __mlxsw_sp_fid_port_vid_map(..., true) and, if the FID has a RIF, maps the egress port/VID (mlxsw_sp_fid_erif_eport_to_vid_map_one). It increments fid_core->port_fid_mappings[local_port] and only on the first mapping of that port (counter was 0) calls mlxsw_sp_port_vp_mode_trans to move the port to virtual mode; so the virtual-mode transition happens on the first mapping, not on every call. On success it returns 0. On a failure of the virtual-mode transition it undoes everything in reverse: decrements the counter, unmaps the egress VID if there is a RIF, unmaps the port/VID, and removes the list entry, then returns the error; failures of the earlier steps undo the steps already done (egress mapping failure undoes the port/VID map and the list entry; port/VID map failure undoes the list entry).
note: Reviewers: original (VP-mode transition only on first mapping) right: 1445; round-2 (error path does not roll back a failed VP-mode transition, only decrements the counter) right in that nothing rolls back the transition itself (it failed) and the counter is decremented: 1453-1454; round-15 (VP-mode failure path also undoes RIF/hardware mappings and list entry, not only counter) right: 1453-1461. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head.

name: mlxsw_sp_fid_nve_flood_index_set
prose: Records an NVE flood index for a FID and programs it (spectrum_fid.c:246-267; the packet item is only the tail of this function, whose name was elided). If fid->nve_flood_index_valid is already true it triggers WARN_ON and returns -EINVAL without changing the FID. Otherwise it stores the flood index in fid->nve_flood_index, sets nve_flood_index_valid, and calls the family's ops->nve_flood_index_set(fid). If that returns an error it clears nve_flood_index_valid again (the stored index value is not cleared) and returns the error; otherwise it returns 0.
note: Item was the tail of mlxsw_sp_fid_nve_flood_index_set; fixed under the real name per rule 6 (read 246-267).

name: mlxsw_sp_router_fib4_replace
prose: Handles an IPv4 FIB route add/replace for the Spectrum router (spectrum_router.c:6815-6873; slice cut the head). It returns 0 without any state change if the route uses a nexthop object (fen_info->fi->nh) that the router does not know. It gets the FIB node for the table, destination and prefix length (a failure warns and returns that error; nothing was created, so no node reference needs releasing), then creates a FIB entry (failure warns, releases the node reference and returns the error). If mlxsw_sp_fib4_allow_replace says the replace is not allowed, it destroys the new entry, puts the node and returns 0, without linking the new entry or destroying the old one. Otherwise it remembers the node's current entry (replaced) and links the new entry (mlxsw_sp_fib_node_entry_link). On a link failure it warns, restores fib_node->fib_entry to the old entry, destroys the new entry, calls mlxsw_sp_fib_node_put and returns the error (whether that put frees the node depends on the node's remaining state, which is decided inside mlxsw_sp_fib_node_put, not read here). On success with no previous entry it returns 0; with a previous entry it clears that entry's hardware flags, destroys it and returns 0.
note: Reviewers: original (omits success path when replace disallowed) right: 6843-6847; round-2 (on fib_node_get failure no entry is created and no node reference released) right: 6831-6834; round-15 (on link failure with a previous entry, fib_node_put returns early so the node ref is not released) unchecked: the put is at 6871 but its early-return behaviour lives in mlxsw_sp_fib_node_put, which I did not read. 2 right, 1 unverified. Slice cut the head.

name: lan966x_handle_fdb
prose: Handles a switchdev FDB add/delete event for a lan966x port (lan966x_fdb.c:253-289; the packet name lan966x_switchdev_event is not the real name and the slice cut the head). It returns 0 immediately if ctx is set and is not this port. For SWITCHDEV_FDB_ADD_TO_DEVICE and SWITCHDEV_FDB_DEL_TO_DEVICE: if orig_dev is a lan966x port and the entry was not added by the user it does nothing (breaks and returns 0). Otherwise it allocates a work item with GFP_ATOMIC (-ENOMEM on failure), fills it (dev, orig_dev, lan966x, event) and copies the fdb_info, allocates a separate 6-byte buffer for the MAC address (on failure it frees the work item and returns -ENOMEM), copies the address and queues the work (lan966x_fdb_event_work) on lan966x->fdb_work; the work handler later frees both allocations. Other events do nothing. It returns 0 except for the two -ENOMEM cases.
note: Packet name wrong; slice cut the head; real function lan966x_handle_fdb (lan966x_fdb.c:253-289). Old reviewers mechanical only (right).

name: sparx5_mact_init
prose: Initialises the Sparx5 MAC table support (sparx5_mactable.c:492-528; slice cut the head). It initialises sparx5->lock, issues the MAC_CMD_CLEAR_ALL table command and waits for it (a timeout/error only logs 'MAC flush error' and continues), sets the default ageing time, learns the broadcast address towards the CPU port group, initialises mdb_lock and the MDB entry list and mact_lock and the MAC entry list, and creates a single-threaded workqueue named '<dev>-mact'. If the workqueue cannot be created it returns -ENOMEM (the mutexes stay initialised and the MAC flush and broadcast learn have already been done). Otherwise it sets up the delayed work sparx5_mact_pull_work, queues it after SPX5_MACT_PULL_DELAY and returns 0.
note: Round-15 reviewer (deinit only destroys mact_lock, not mdb_lock, so it cannot release all initialised mutexes) is about sparx5_mact_deinit, which I did not read; not checked. This function initialises sparx5->lock, mdb_lock and mact_lock (496, 513, 515). Slice cut the head; real function 492-528.

name: sparx5_init_coreclock
prose: Chooses and programs the core clock of a Sparx5/LAN969x switch (sparx5_main.c:478-629; the packet name sparx5_core_clock_set is not the real name; the slice shows only part of it). The requested frequency is sparx5->coreclock. By sparx5->target_ct it resolves SPX5_CORE_CLOCK_DEFAULT to the highest supported frequency (250 MHz for 7546, 500 MHz for 7549/7552/7556, 625 MHz for 7558/7558TSN and the TSN variants) and marks an unsupported explicit request as frequency 0; all LAN969x targets are forced to 328 MHz; an unknown target logs and returns -ENODEV. For a real Sparx5 (is_sparx5) the frequency must be 250, 500 or 625 MHz (clk_div 10/5/4, pol_upd_int 312/624/780), otherwise it logs and returns -EINVAL; for those it writes the LCPLL core clock config; for a LAN969x it uses pol_upd_int 820. It then stores the chosen frequency in sparx5->coreclock, computes the clock period and writes it into the HSCH system clock (Sparx5 only), the two policer DLB control registers, the learn auto-age config, each GCB SIO clock, the TAS revisit delay and the policer update interval, and returns 0.
note: Packet name wrong; real function sparx5_init_coreclock (478-629), read in full. The slice contained other functions too (qlim_set, board_init, start, start of probe). Old reviewers mechanical only (right).

name: mchp_sparx5_probe
prose: Platform-driver probe for the Microchip Sparx5/LAN969x switch (sparx5_main.c:781-1010; slice cut the head). It returns -ENODEV, -ENOMEM or -EINVAL directly for missing device-tree/platform data, a failed sparx5 allocation, or missing match data, the error of dev_err_probe for a failed reset lookup, and -ENODEV for a missing ports node, before any cleanup label. Later steps set err and jump: cleanup_pnode (early failures), cleanup_config (config parsing, register mapping, hardware identification, switchcore/core clock/RAM init, port creation), cleanup_ports (sparx5_start, QoS, VCAP init), cleanup_vcap (MAC table init), cleanup_mact (stats init), cleanup_stats (PTP init), cleanup_ptp (netdev registration) and cleanup_netdevs (notifier registration). The cleanup chain runs in reverse: unregister netdevs, ptp deinit, stats deinit, MAC table deinit, VCAP deinit, destroy netdevs, kfree(configs), of_node_put(ports). The chain does not call sparx5_unregister_notifier_blocks (the failing step there is the registration itself). On success it does not return directly: it jumps to cleanup_config, which frees the temporary configs and releases the ports node, and returns err, which is 0 at that point.
note: Reviewer (cleanup never calls sparx5_unregister_notifier_blocks despite annotation claiming notifier blocks unregistered) is right: the labels 993-1009 contain no such call. Slice cut the head. I read the tail (940-1010) and the goto/label structure; I did not read the middle (hardware init and port creation, about 833-940) line by line.

name: ocelot_chain_to_block
prose: Maps a tc-flower chain number to an Ocelot VCAP block (ocelot_flower.c:28-57). With ingress false it returns VCAP_ES0 for chain 0 and -EOPNOTSUPP for every other chain (so no IS1, IS2 or PSFP chain is accepted on egress). With ingress true, chain 0 returns VCAP_IS2 (backwards compatibility); a chain equal to VCAP_IS1_CHAIN(lookup) for some IS1 lookup returns VCAP_IS1; a chain equal to VCAP_IS2_CHAIN(lookup, pag) for some IS2 lookup and PAG value returns VCAP_IS2 (only those discrete combinations, not a contiguous numeric range); OCELOT_PSFP_CHAIN returns PSFP_BLOCK_ID; any other chain returns -EOPNOTSUPP. It has no side effects.
note: Contract left empty: the numeric values of VCAP_ES0, VCAP_IS1, VCAP_IS2 and PSFP_BLOCK_ID come from enums/macros outside the file, and the old contract also hard-coded numeric chain ranges that I could not confirm. Reviewers: round-1 (IS2 chains are the discrete (lookup, pag) set, not a contiguous 20000-21255 range) consistent with the code at 48-51; round-2 (prose omits that IS1/PSFP chains with ingress=false return -EOPNOTSUPP) right: 32-36. 2 right.

name: myri10ge_alloc_slices
prose: Allocates the per-slice state of a myri10ge NIC (myri10ge.c:3582-3618; slice cut the head). It allocates mgp->ss, an array of num_slices myri10ge_slice_state, zeroed, returning -ENOMEM if that fails. For each slice it allocates a coherent DMA ring of max_intr_slots receive-done entries and a coherent DMA buffer for the firmware statistics (a failure of either goes to abort), sets the slice's back pointers to mgp and the net_device and adds its NAPI context with myri10ge_poll and the configured weight. On success it returns 0. At abort it calls myri10ge_free_slices(mgp) (which frees what was allocated so far) and returns -ENOMEM.
note: Slice cut the head; real function 3582-3618. Old prose unreviewed; rechecked against the source (note NAPI added only for slices that were fully allocated).

name: myri10ge_probe_slices
prose: Decides how many slices (RSS queues) the myri10ge NIC will use (myri10ge.c:3626-3746; returns nothing). It first sets mgp->num_slices = 1 and returns right away (leaving 1) if the module limit myri10ge_max_slices is 1, the device has no MSI-X capability, or the limit is -1 and fewer than 2 default RSS queues are available. Otherwise it swaps in the RSS firmware name (the module override, or the RSS variant of the aligned/unaligned firmware) and loads it; if that load fails it logs 'Rss firmware not found', frees the old firmware name if it was allocated and returns with the RSS firmware name left in mgp->fw_name (the old name is not restored on this path). It then resets the board, reads the interrupt-queue slot count, sets the interrupt queue size and queries the maximum RSS queues; failures, or myri10ge_msi being off, go to abort_with_fw. It caps the slice count at the module limit (or the CPU count when the limit is -1), allocates the MSI-X vector table (failure goes to no_msix) and then tries pci_enable_msix_range with a power-of-two slice count, reducing it when fewer vectors are available. A successful allocation is immediately released with pci_disable_msix (MSI-X is not left enabled) and the function returns with the RSS firmware and the chosen slice count; the old firmware name is freed if it was allocated. If MSI-X cannot be used it frees msix_vectors at no_msix; then at abort_with_fw it sets num_slices back to 1, restores the old firmware name and reloads that firmware.
note: Reviewers: original (early rss firmware load failure returns without restoring old fw_name) right: 3656-3661; round-2 (on success pci_disable_msix is called before returning, so MSI-X is not left enabled) right: 3725-3730. 2/2 right. Slice cut the head; real function 3626-3746, read in full.
